findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the ceil(eff_max_iter/2) formula-consumer inventory via find_referencing_symbols on build_usage_limits plus a grep for the formula, reconcile completion_banking.py:plan_recovery_pool's `math.ceil(floor / 2)` encoding with the census, and either list it as an intentionally-unaffected second encoding or adjust the source-census test's 'no other module encodes the bare formula' assertion accordingly.
evidence: Plan: 'The one control-flow consumer is workflow/completion_banking.py:iteration_limit_for, which inverts it as iteration_limit = 2×B'
Plan: 'A source-census test asserts ... that no other module encodes the bare formula.'
completion_banking.py:243 `n = math.ceil(floor / 2)` with docstring l.229-230: 'N is the primary's per-run request budget as build_usage_limits computes it — ceil(eff_max_iter / 2)'
findings.finding: The formula census names iteration_limit_for as 'the one control-flow consumer' of ceil(eff_max_iter/2) and its source-census test asserts 'no other module encodes the bare formula', but completion_banking.py:plan_recovery_pool (line 243, `n = math.ceil(floor / 2)`) independently encodes the same ceil(x/2) request-budget formula — its own docstring ties it to build_usage_limits' `ceil(eff_max_iter / 2)`. The inventory of formula encodings is incomplete and appears hand-enumerated rather than symbol-graph-derived (a find_referencing_symbols/find_symbol sweep of build_usage_limits and the formula would surface plan_recovery_pool).
findings.location: Scope → 'Cross-directory consumers of the ceil(eff_max_iter/2) formula' and the source-census test bullet
scenarios: completion_banking.py:plan_recovery_pool re-encodes ceil(floor/2) as the recovery-pool N; the source-census test's 'no other module encodes the bare formula' assertion fails against it, or is silently hand-waived, leaving a real second formula site unreviewed and un-reconciled with the S2 combined-allowance change.
If build_usage_limits' base-vs-allowance split ever needs to flow to the successor-pool sizing, plan_recovery_pool is the site that would need it and it is absent from the census.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the census to name both formula encodings in completion_banking.py (iteration_limit_for AND plan_recovery_pool's `n = math.ceil(floor / 2)`), state explicitly why plan_recovery_pool is unaffected by the base+allowance split (same rationale as iteration_limit_for: it consumes the bare base), and scope the source-census test to the returned req_limit rather than asserting no other module encodes the formula.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the new `pai_retry` operation guard translates a transient `finish_reason='error'` StructuredOutputError into `ModelRetry` (as S1's `guard_capability` does), so it draws a shared-budget in-run retry rather than aborting the operation as a non-`ModelRetry` exception.
evidence: Plan: 'a transient `error` raises the retryable `StructuredOutputError`'
pai_output.py:80-81 (landed S1): `except StructuredOutputError as err: raise ModelRetry(str(err)) from err`
guard_capability docstring: transient error 'is translated into Pydantic AI's ModelRetry ... so Pydantic AI drives its own bounded retry instead of aborting on a non-ModelRetry exception'
A non-ModelRetry exception propagates out of the agent loop and aborts the run — it cannot be 'retryable' without the ModelRetry translation
findings.finding: Plan step 2(b) specifies the operation guard makes a transient finish_reason='error' 'raise the retryable StructuredOutputError', but the landed S1 guard translates that same StructuredOutputError into ModelRetry so pydantic-ai retries rather than aborts; raising a bare StructuredOutputError (a non-ModelRetry) would abort the run after one call, contradicting 'retryable' and diverging from the S1 contract the plan is composing.
scenarios: A provider returns finish_reason='error' on the first turn; under the plan-as-written the guard raises a bare StructuredOutputError and the whole operation aborts instead of consuming a shared-budget retry
findings.suggested_fix: In step 2(b) and the pai_retry scope, state the guard delegates to structured.check_response and, on the retryable StructuredOutputError it raises, re-raises `ModelRetry(str(err)) from err` (mirroring pai_output.guard_capability) so the transient-error path stays an in-run retry consuming the shared counter; only refusal/content_filter (UnretryableOutputError) propagates terminally.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify whether the truncation reclassification consults the SAME two-layer truncation signal set (normalized finish_reason AND provider_details) that check_response uses, so a length/max_tokens signal appearing only in provider_details still yields the bounded concision ModelRetry rather than terminal UnretryableOutputError.
evidence: Plan: 'on `finish_reason` `length`/`max_tokens`, before parsing, raises ... ModelRetry(...); (b) otherwise delegates to `structured.check_response(response)`'
structured.py:632 `_UNRETRYABLE_STOP_REASONS = frozenset({"refusal", "max_tokens", "length", "content_filter"})`

structured.py:663-679 check_response layer-2 checks `provider_details` `finish_reason` against `_UNRETRYABLE_STOP_REASONS` and raises UnretryableOutputError — 'catches a refusal even if a future adapter stops mapping it onto finish_reason (leaving it None/stop)'
findings.finding: The concision reclassification decision rule only inspects normalized finish_reason, but structured.check_response is a documented TWO-LAYER guard that ALSO treats a raw length/max_tokens (or refusal) signal in response.provider_details as terminal UnretryableOutputError. A truncation surfaced only in provider_details (the pydantic-ai #5221 shape layer 2 defends against) would bypass the plan's reclassification and be delegated to check_response as terminal, defeating the intended bounded concision retry.
findings.location: Approach step 2 (Truncation reclassification guard); AC line 'length/max_tokens consumes at most the configured output-retry allowance'
scenarios: A provider/adapter that surfaces truncation only in provider_details (finish_reason None/stop) — a concision-eligible truncation is instead classified terminal and gets no bounded retry
findings.suggested_fix: State that the operation guard reclassifies on the same truncation-signal detection check_response applies (both finish_reason and provider_details['finish_reason']), routing any max_tokens/length signal — regardless of layer — to the concision ModelRetry before delegating the remaining (refusal/content_filter/error) cases to check_response.
